concern_ledger_updates.reason: The actor expressly concedes there is no admissible evidence that final pre-launch model-card disclosure was completed.
The actor concedes the available risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, unapproved, and does not address the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment.

The response narrows the claim to conditional or caveated compliance, but supplies no evidence that the condition was satisfied or that certification was formally recorded as contingent before launch.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence. The response is a narrower interpretation of the same record and, if anything, reinforces the existing gaps by conceding that the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment remains in scope, the rollout controls do not exclude it, the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete, and there is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure was completed before launch. Under the policy text, disclosure or approved risk acceptance is a compliance predicate, not a mere caveat. Because that predicate remains unproven, the record supports at most a conditional path to compliance, not compliant or compliant_with_caveats as an already satisfied state.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the required pre-launch model-card disclosure of the Spanish-language billing support limitation was actually completed.
The only risk-acceptance evidence remains an incomplete draft with no approver and no coverage of the exposed Spanish-language billing support segment.
The narrowed caveated position still depends on a compliance predicate that is not yet evidenced; it describes a possible path to compliance, not proof that compliance was achieved.
The actor's requested shift to caveated compliance is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new admissible evidence closing the disclosure or approval gaps.
